Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.

summary.latency_aggregation: No pooled request latency quantiles are computed: individual report schemas 1, 2 and 3 contain histogram quantile summaries, not mergeable bucket counts. Latency statistics describe distributions of per-trial successful/failed p50/p95/p99 values, conditional on trials with those observations; their means are not pooled request quantiles.
methodology: A seeded permutation of condition indices is rotated by one position each round. Within each complete block of N rounds, every condition occupies every round position once. An incomplete block is only partially balanced; this rotating Latin order does not balance all predecessor/successor pairs.

The order seed controls only the condition schedule. Effective workload seeds and all other configuration values remain unchanged. Each entry executes one fresh sequential batch trial with persisted-report integrity and cleanup checks.

Further trials require verified individual evidence and successful cleanup, or verified evidence that no environment was provisioned. Unsafe cleanup, missing evidence, cancellation and summary-write failures stop execution; all remaining planned entries stay explicitly unstarted.

Failed and partial trials with valid evidence and safe cleanup remain in their condition statistics. Timing statistics are conditional on observed milestones; missing and censored observations are not zero-duration events. Request latency quantiles are not pooled across trials or conditions.

Condition summaries reuse batch aggregation. Condition-summary report paths are relative to their own summary directory; schedule report paths and batch references are relative to the comparison directory. Host and environment references point to individual JSON report sections.

Ordering reduces systematic position confounding but does not prove causality, independent samples, equal host conditions or population reliability. Compare individual environmental metadata and actual order before interpreting differences.

summary.latency_aggregation: No pooled request latency quantiles are computed: individual report schemas 1, 2 and 3 contain histogram quantile summaries, not mergeable bucket counts. Latency statistics describe distributions of per-trial successful/failed p50/p95/p99 values, conditional on trials with those observations; their means are not pooled request quantiles.
methodology: A seeded permutation of condition indices is rotated by one position each round. Within each complete block of N rounds, every condition occupies every round position once. An incomplete block is only partially balanced; this rotating Latin order does not balance all predecessor/successor pairs.

The order seed controls only the condition schedule. Effective workload seeds and all other configuration values remain unchanged. Each entry executes one fresh sequential batch trial with persisted-report integrity and cleanup checks.

Further trials require verified individual evidence and successful cleanup, or verified evidence that no environment was provisioned. Unsafe cleanup, missing evidence, cancellation and summary-write failures stop execution; all remaining planned entries stay explicitly unstarted.

Failed and partial trials with valid evidence and safe cleanup remain in their condition statistics. Timing statistics are conditional on observed milestones; missing and censored observations are not zero-duration events. Request latency quantiles are not pooled across trials or conditions.

Condition summaries reuse batch aggregation. Condition-summary report paths are relative to their own summary directory; schedule report paths and batch references are relative to the comparison directory. Host and environment references point to individual JSON report sections.

Ordering reduces systematic position confounding but does not prove causality, independent samples, equal host conditions or population reliability. Compare individual environmental metadata and actual order before interpreting differences.

write_stages.methodology: Diagnostic SET and WAIT stages are excluded from logical request and pacing counts. SET latency includes routing, pool/connection initialization and handled redirections before its terminal result; WAIT latency covers only an attempted WAIT call on the same physical connection. Logical set_wait latency covers the complete write executor operation. A short integer WAIT reply has policy error class wait_short, distinct from client timeout. No WAIT stage is recorded when it cannot start; integer acknowledgement histograms exclude errors. Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Every successful client SET acknowledgement is validated, including writes whose subsequent WAIT returned too few replica acknowledgements or an error. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. The WAIT-satisfied subset is reported separately and does not imply disk durability or loss-free failover. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a durability guarantee.

summary.latency_aggregation: No pooled request latency quantiles are computed: individual report schemas 1, 2 and 3 contain histogram quantile summaries, not mergeable bucket counts. Latency statistics describe distributions of per-trial successful/failed p50/p95/p99 values, conditional on trials with those observations; their means are not pooled request quantiles.
methodology: A seeded permutation of condition indices is rotated by one position each round. Within each complete block of N rounds, every condition occupies every round position once. An incomplete block is only partially balanced; this rotating Latin order does not balance all predecessor/successor pairs.

The order seed controls only the condition schedule. Effective workload seeds and all other configuration values remain unchanged. Each entry executes one fresh sequential batch trial with persisted-report integrity and cleanup checks.

Further trials require verified individual evidence and successful cleanup, or verified evidence that no environment was provisioned. Unsafe cleanup, missing evidence, cancellation and summary-write failures stop execution; all remaining planned entries stay explicitly unstarted.

Failed and partial trials with valid evidence and safe cleanup remain in their condition statistics. Timing statistics are conditional on observed milestones; missing and censored observations are not zero-duration events. Request latency quantiles are not pooled across trials or conditions.

Condition summaries reuse batch aggregation. Condition-summary report paths are relative to their own summary directory; schedule report paths and batch references are relative to the comparison directory. Host and environment references point to individual JSON report sections.

Ordering reduces systematic position confounding but does not prove causality, independent samples, equal host conditions or population reliability. Compare individual environmental metadata and actual order before interpreting differences.

write_stages.methodology: Diagnostic SET and WAIT stages are excluded from logical request and pacing counts. SET latency includes routing, pool/connection initialization and handled redirections before its terminal result; WAIT latency covers only an attempted WAIT call on the same physical connection. Logical set_wait latency covers the complete write executor operation. A short integer WAIT reply has policy error class wait_short, distinct from client timeout. No WAIT stage is recorded when it cannot start; integer acknowledgement histograms exclude errors. Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Every successful client SET acknowledgement is validated, including writes whose subsequent WAIT returned too few replica acknowledgements or an error. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. The WAIT-satisfied subset is reported separately and does not imply disk durability or loss-free failover. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a durability guarantee.

Logical set_wait latency covers the complete write executor operation. A short integer WAIT reply has policy error class wait_short, distinct from client timeout. No WAIT stage is recorded when it cannot start; integer acknowledgement histograms exclude errors. Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Every successful client SET acknowledgement is validated, including writes whose subsequent WAIT returned too few replica acknowledgements or an error. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. The WAIT-satisfied subset is reported separately and does not imply disk durability or loss-free failover. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a durability guarantee.

methodology: A seeded permutation of condition indices is rotated by one position each round. Within each complete block of N rounds, every condition occupies every round position once. An incomplete block is only partially balanced; this rotating Latin order does not balance all predecessor/successor pairs.

The order seed controls only the condition schedule. Effective workload seeds and all other configuration values remain unchanged. Each entry executes one fresh sequential batch trial with persisted-report integrity and cleanup checks.

Further trials require verified individual evidence and successful cleanup, or verified evidence that no environment was provisioned. Unsafe cleanup, missing evidence, cancellation and summary-write failures stop execution; all remaining planned entries stay explicitly unstarted.

Failed and partial trials with valid evidence and safe cleanup remain in their condition statistics. Timing statistics are conditional on observed milestones; missing and censored observations are not zero-duration events. Request latency quantiles are not pooled across trials or conditions.

Condition summaries reuse batch aggregation. Condition-summary report paths are relative to their own summary directory; schedule report paths and batch references are relative to the comparison directory. Host and environment references point to individual JSON report sections.

Ordering reduces systematic position confounding but does not prove causality, independent samples, equal host conditions or population reliability. Compare individual environmental metadata and actual order before interpreting differences.
